title: The relationship between the coarticulatory source and effect in sound change: evidence from Italo-Romance metaphony in the Lausberg area
why_promising: Primary production from 35 speakers in three Southern Italian varieties; 5,372 analysed mid-vowel tokens after exclusions. Speech was MAUS-segmented and F1/F2 tracked at 5-ms frame shift, with around 40% manually corrected for misplaced boundaries or mistracked formants. The public secondary deposit contains analysis dataframes plus lexical/stem/consonantal metadata; the underlying EMU acoustic database and Speakers.xlsx are documented but embargoed until 2039.
open_question: Determine whether the open analysis dataframes identify which individual tokens received manual boundary/formant correction so a clean human-corrected subset can be isolated. Do not admit the unflagged forced-aligned remainder. If correction flags are absent, retain as review/source reference despite final trajectories. Inventory Secondary_dataset.zip when binary retrieval is available.
